items.title: Former rural road set for major widening to improve traffic flow in Mississauga
items.summary: Traffic flow is expected to improve significantly along one of Mississauga’s former rural roads as a major widening project transforms Ninth Line into a much larger thoroughfare, adding travel lanes, cycling infrastructure and sidewalks to accommodate the area’s growing population. The work will expand Ninth Line between Eglinton Avenue and Derry Road. This stretch has seen considerable residential development in recent years and is expected to handle increasing numbers of commuters as more neighbourhoods take shape. According to Mississauga Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden, construction is progressing along the corridor, with crews working on road improvements, underground infrastructure, sidewalks and cycling facilities. The completed roadway will feature two travel lanes in each direction, along with raised medians or centre-turning lanes. The project will also install protected cycling tracks and separate sidewalks on both sides of the road. The improvements are intended to do more than simply move additional vehicles through the area. They will also provide safer options for cyclists and pedestrians while making room for future public transit service, according to McFadden. In a recent update posted on her website, McFadden outlined several completed and ongoing construction activities on the route. Temporary traffic and pedestrian signals had been activated at several intersections, including Eglinton Avenue, Burdette Terrace, Henrietta Drive, Thomas Street, Erin Centre Boulevard and Britannia Road. Crews had also completed curb work between Eglinton Avenue and Britannia Road, with much of the sidewalk and concrete work substantially finished. Bus pads at Skyview Street and Erin Centre Boulevard were also completed.

items.title: Mississauga teen identified as victim of fatal shooting in Etobicoke
items.summary: An 18-year-old from Mississauga has been identified as the victim of a fatal shooting in Etobicoke on Saturday afternoon. m. on Saturday (Nov. 7). Officers found a man who had been shot. Life-saving measures were performed, and he was taken to hospital by paramedics, where he was pronounced dead. The suspect or suspects fled the area before police arrived. Police have identified the victim as Malik Abass, 18, of Mississauga, and have released his photo. Toronto police’s Homicide and Missing Persons Unit is investigating. Police have not released a suspect description or said what led to the shooting. The area is in central Etobicoke, close to the Mississauga border. Police say it is Toronto’s 33rd homicide of 2026.

items.title: Students can explore programs and campus life at Sheridan College open house in Mississauga
items.summary: Prospective college students will have an opportunity to explore their options, meet instructors and get a firsthand look at campus life when Sheridan College hosts an open house in Mississauga later this week. The event will take place Thursday, Nov. 12, at Sheridan’s Hazel McCallion Campus, giving students a chance to discover what the school has to offer before deciding where to pursue their post-secondary education. , the open house is designed to help visitors get a better understanding of the programs available at the Mississauga campus and what they can expect as Sheridan students. Visitors will be able to tour the campus, explore classrooms, labs and student spaces, and connect with faculty members and current students. The interactive sessions will also give prospective students an opportunity to learn more about individual programs, ask questions and discuss potential career paths. The event will also provide an opportunity to learn about the practical considerations of attending college, including financial assistance and student services. Representatives will be available to discuss options such as OSAP, scholarships, bursaries, awards and work-study opportunities. Prospective students can also get information about the support available through Sheridan’s Student Affairs department, including health and wellness services, housing, accessible learning, tutoring and student advising. Sheridan operates three campuses in the region, but each offers a different selection of programs. The college encourages prospective students to attend the open house at the campus where their preferred program is offered. For those considering Sheridan, the open house offers a chance to look beyond course descriptions and websites and see the learning environment for themselves. Visitors can get a feel for the classrooms and facilities, talk to people who teach and study there, and determine whether the campus and its programs are a good fit.

items.title: Diwali fireworks: Where they’re allowed and banned across the GTA tonight
items.summary: “Fireworks are not permitted on balconies, beaches, streets, parking lots or in parks,” Toronto Fire Services reminded residents on Sunday (Nov. 8), as families across the GTA celebrate Diwali. “Make sure you know where fireworks are allowed before using them,” the fire service said in a social media post. For many families, fireworks are part of the Diwali tradition. But the rules depend on where you live, and in some cities, setting off fireworks could lead to a hefty fine. m. m. without a permit. The city will have extra bylaw officers on duty after receiving a record 432 fireworks complaints during Diwali last year. Fireworks allowed without permit on one night as Diwali celebrated in Mississauga Brampton bans the use, sale and possession of all fireworks, with sparklers the only exception. Discharging or possessing fireworks without a permit carries a $500 fine, and selling them brings a $1,000 fine. The city may also issue a court summons, with fines ranging from $500 to $100,000. Property owners can also be charged if fireworks are set off on their land. Instead, the city hosts its own fireworks displays at city-led Diwali events.

items.title: Measles exposure at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Travellers who passed through Toronto Pearson International Airport last week may have been exposed to measles, Durham Region health officials say. The Durham Region Health Department has identified more public exposure sites linked to a confirmed measles case in an unimmunized child from the region who had recently travelled internationally. Anyone who was at these locations should watch for symptoms until Nov. 24. The health department says it has followed up directly with known contacts in Durham Region. People who may have been exposed are advised to make sure they and their families have had two doses of measles vaccine (MMR or MMRV). Those born before 1970 likely had measles as children and are considered protected. Anyone unsure of their vaccination status should check with their health-care provider. Anyone who develops symptoms should stay home from work or school and call ahead before visiting a clinic or doctor, so staff can prepare and prevent the virus from spreading. They should also wear a well-fitting mask when getting medical care. Measles is highly contagious and spreads easily among people who aren’t immunized or haven’t had the disease. The virus can stay in the air or on surfaces for up to two hours. Symptoms usually appear seven to 21 days after infection and can include a high fever, cough, runny nose, red and watery eyes, sensitivity to light, and a red rash lasting four to seven days.

items.title: Streetsville Barbershop Owner Turns Walls Into Gallery for Local Artists and His Own Paintings
items.summary: A Streetsville barbershop called Heartbreak Hotel has become more than a place for haircuts, doubling as a showcase for local art and streetwear. According to the Toronto Star, owner Omar Preza, 44, was born in El Salvador and raised in Canada, and built the shop around his lifelong passions for drawing, comic books and street graffiti. The newspaper reported that customers walk in to upbeat Latin and hip-hop music, with painted canvases in thrifted gold frames and custom apparel hanging from industrial pipe racks against black-and-white brick walls. The Star said Heartbreak Hotel began in 2013 as a streetwear clothing brand, with Preza starting to paint around the same time, and today he sells both his original fine art and custom-designed apparel in the shop alongside the haircuts. His work was included in the Art Gallery of Mississauga's 2024-2025 Fourth Annual Juried Show of Visual Arts, according to the paper.

items.title: Budget-Priced Danish Retailer Set to Open Square One Location Next Week
items.summary: A Danish variety chain known for quirky, low-cost home goods is set to open its first Mississauga location at Square One Shopping Centre on Saturday, Nov. 14. According to insauga.com, Flying Tiger Copenhagen will open a sister store at CF Markville in Markham two days earlier, on Nov. 12. The outlet reported the retailer stocks home decor, stationery, toys, kitchenware, party supplies and seasonal items, with more than 80 per cent of its products priced under $10. Roughly 300 new items arrive in its stores each month, insauga.com said. The chain traces its roots to Copenhagen in 1995, when it launched under the name Tiger, and now runs more than 1,000 stores across 45 markets, with Canada becoming its 45th this year. Its first Canadian store opened at CF Toronto Eaton Centre in June, and the company has said the GTA marks its first step into a wider rollout across the Americas. CEO Jens Aarup Mikkelsen said in a release that the company sees strong alignment with Canadian shoppers who want design-led products at accessible prices. Stores are laid out like a maze so customers pass through all 14 product categories, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Dixie Road Tops List as Nearly 300 Vehicles Stolen Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Month
items.summary: Peel Regional Police data shows thieves stole 283 vehicles across Mississauga and Brampton between Oct. 7 and Nov. 7, averaging about nine thefts a day. According to insauga.com, Mississauga accounted for 167 of those thefts while Brampton saw 116. The outlet reported that cars made up the bulk of the stolen vehicles, with 201 automobiles taken alongside 60 trucks, 17 motorcycles and five vehicles in other categories. In Mississauga, Dixie Road saw the most thefts with 10 reported, followed by nine on Airport Road, five on Argentia Road, four on Britannia Road and three in the City Centre area. Brampton's hot spots included seven thefts on Great Lakes Drive and four each on Bramtree Court and Coventry Road, insauga.com said. Peel police are asking anyone with information to call 905-453-3311 or contact Peel Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS.
